genius cleaning products! at vamoosh, our aim is simple, to invent and develop innovative laundry and cleaning products that solve those little, often annoying, everyday problems. our journey began with vamoosh pet hair dissolver, after years of development and testing. designed to tackle one of the most frustrating household challenges, pet hair in the wash, it quickly became the foundation of the vamoosh range. since then, vamoosh has grown into a broader collection of clever cleaning solutions. from washing machine and dishwasher care to toilet, drain, and fabric innovations, including limited edition launches, our products are made to work hard and deliver real results. backed by the expertise of the team at cares laboratory, we combine innovation, manufacturing know-how, and strong brand thinking built over decades in the industry. everything we do is driven by practical problem-solving, with a genuine understanding of real homes and the everyday mess that comes with them. vamoosh is here to help make everyday cleaning simpler and more effective. happy vamooshing! the inspiration for vamoosh pet hair dissolver came from family pet, mr chips (pictured here). as much as we love mr chips, his pet shedding was causing a never-ending hairy problem in our household - particularly when it came to washing his dog pet bedding and dog blankets in the washing machine. the hair would always stick to the bedding - and the washing machine would end up clogged up with pet hair (and if there's anything worse than pet hair it's wet pet hair!!) that's when the idea for vamoosh pet hair dissolver was born!! after years in the laboratory, we came up with vamoosh pet hair dissolver. following on from our innovative laundry product, we then came up with the idea of vamoosh washing machine cleaner - and we have plenty of other innovations in development, so watch this space! here's a pic of the lovely lynsey queen of clean! we have wonderful supporters of vamoosh including lynsey queen of clean who uses our products regularly. we love hearing your feedback! you can either email us at care@careslaboratory.com or find us on instagram or facebook @vamooshcleans. we love to hear your views and especially love to see pictures of your furbabies… cruelty free we are proud to display the peta-approved logo to show that vamoosh is a cruelty-free brand and to raise awareness that innovative and quality products such as vamoosh can be made without the need for harming animals. you can find out more about the people for the ethical treatment of animals (peta) foundation. charity partnerships as our team has grown, our love for animals has too. it was important to us to show our support for support dogs as what they do is truly life changing. support dogs is a national charity dedicated to transforming the lives of children and adults affected by autism, epilepsy, and physical disabilities. as well as donating money to the charity, vamoosh will be giving an unlimited supply of pet hair dissolver to all the dog owners and to the centre themselves. vamoosh are determined to raise awareness, especially within the cleaning community for their hard work and ultimately gather more donations so that support dogs can continue to help adults and children across the nation. to find out more click the logo. newsletter subscribe to our newsletter to keep up to date with everything vamoosh! is a method of metal cutting that uses a high-powered laser to vaporise and cut metal. laser cutting is most commonly used for industrial applications, but can also be used to create bespoke laser etching and engraving. what materials can be laser cut? a multitude of materials can be laser cut to suit a range of purposes and applications, including a range of metals. what materials can’t be laser cut? although the majority of materials can be laser cut, some materials are not recommended for laser cutting. some of these materials include fibreglass, polycarbonate, pvc and hdpe. how does laser cutting work? laser cutting involves focusing a laser beam through a lens onto the material to be cut. the intense heat of the laser beam melts or vaporizes the material along the desired cutting path, creating a narrow kerf. computer-controlled movements guide the laser beam, allowing for intricate and precise cuts. what are the advantages of laser cutting? there are several advantages to using laser cutting, some of which include: cuts non-ferrous materials easily rapid turn around can cut through metals up to 50mm thick capable of cutting highly-detailed and precise cutting include: fusion cutting – a cutting technique that cuts metal by melting them and then blowing out the molten remnants using a high-pressure stream of inert gas. remote cutting: involves pub accounts and pub stocktaking, we are now the premium choice across the hospitality industry for accounts, payroll, stocktaking and business planning all under one umbrella. our clients range from small pubs to large gastropubs, restaurants, takeaways, pub companies and hotel groups. whatever the size of your business, or the size of your ambition, roslyns can support you. ​ we look after businesses of all sizes across the uk based from our offices in sheffield and our national network of business development managers and stocktakers. ​ our business development managers are highly trained and experienced in multiple aspects of business and in particular the hospitality industry. they are also trained in all aspects of the pubs code including mro. our roslyns bdms fulfill a contact us and the right person will be in touch. to mark our 30th anniversary we would like to introduce you to our company founder, martin roslyn. you can watch this short video clip where we hear about martin's first job, the changes in the hospitality industry he has steered roslyns through and where he sees the company going next. robbie stewart ​ commercial operations director i live in a small village in north yorkshire with my wife. i've worked in the hospitality industry all of my life in a range of roles from manager, multi-site operations manager and business owner. i have been with roslyns for 9 years now and love working for a company so focused on making things better for our clients in what is a tough industry. outside of work i enjoy live music, woodworking and riding my motorbike. mark owen ​ operations director i live in the small market town of desborough, northamptonshire with my wife, three children and murray the cat. i have worked in the hospitality industry for 30 year including nine years as a publican. i have been with roslyns for 9 years. i enjoy watching my son play football for two teams and days out with the family as long as they include stopping at a pub. ben darwin head of business development i am originally from leeds but now live in the lovely city of york with my wife, 2 daughters and our dog. i have been in the licence trade industry for the best part of 25 years. i have worked in and managed a variety of venues, from back street boozers to town centre bars, hotels and golf clubs. i spent over 10 years of this as a stocktaker and festival in york. lee goodship ​ senior business development manager i live in the market town of malmesbury (where you will find england's oldest hotel!) with my wife, children and lab george. i have worked in the hospitality industry for 27 years starting out as a chef in the savoy to a range of management and multi-site roles also having run my own pub restaurants. i have been with roslyns for 7 years. outside of work i love live music/festivals, spending quality time with my family, country walks with george, playing squash and searching for new gins to add to my ever-growing collection! daniel watson ​ business development manager i live in a market town on the border of shropshire with my wife and our labrador rupert. i have worked in the hospitality industry for 20 years, of scotland, with my wife and two working dogs. i'm a passionate pub, restaurant, hotel and catering specialist with a broad commercial knowledge. i've held positions covering all of scotland and north of england as an area and operations manager, having worked within the hospitality industry for over 30 years, 12 of these years as an independent hotelier. outside of work i enjoy the great outdoors and all that it has to offer. russell furlong business development manager i live in the northumberland town of ashington with my partner and our german shepherd cross alaskan malamute dog bear. i also have a 10-year-old daughter who is my world. i have worked in the hospitality industry for 23 years working in various roles in branded and unbranded pub restaurants, for most of these minibus into an off-grid campervan. i have most recently taken up woodworking and have made a couple of cabinets and a shelving unit to date. jonathan watson business development manager i live in tamworth (central to everywhere), with my partner, and my daughter. i have worked in the hospitality industry for 12 years starting out as bar staff. for 7 years i worked in hotels working different roles before becoming a conference & events manager. i worked for roslyns as a stock auditor for 3 years before making the move to business development manager in 2022. outside of work i love spending time with my family and following my football team aston villa around the country. (usually losing). martin leman business development manager originally from normandy (france) i have lived in bexleyheath since 1998. i have worked in the hospitality industry for 17 years, including hotel and bar manager roles at the connaught hotel in mayfair, metropolitan hotel and mandeville hotel. i was also the restaurant/owner of chez sophie at the harrow near sevenoaks, for six years. outside of work i enjoy kitesurfing, playing the piano and riding my motorcycle on the open roads, but most of all spending time with my daughter and son. laura scott business development manager i live in the heart of the lake district with my husband, 3 kids, 2 dogs and a bearded dragon. i have worked in and alongside the hospitality industry for over 20 years including events and bar management, wine sales and waste management. venues i have worked in range from 5-star hotels and resorts to local pubs and a rugby club. outside of work i spend most of my time ferry my children to dance, rugby, football, and air cadets but when i do get the odd bit of time for me, i enjoy paddleboarding and walking. i am also appearing in my first pantomime this year (oh yes i am)! lois barreto business development manager i live in fen drayton, a small cambridgeshire village with my husband and three children. i have worked in the hospitality industry for nearly 20 years, starting as a chalet host in val thorens, then as a purser on cruise ships. for the last 10 years i have worked as a publican. in my spare time i love caravanning with my family, reading and most recently running. i ran my first half marathon at the beginning of the year and have already booked my next one! bottom of page

and minimize downtime from workplace incidents. what is lone working? lone working describes any job role where an employee performs their duties without direct supervision or coworkers nearby. this can include healthcare professionals, retail associates, construction workers, real estate agents, delivery drivers, and utility workers. because there’s no immediate help on-site, lone workers face greater safety risks, including workplace accidents, sudden health emergencies, or encounters with aggressive individuals. in these situations, response time can mean the difference between a close call and a serious incident. employers can reduce these risks by implementing a lone worker safety solution, such as a discreet wearable device or a lone worker safety app with gps tracking, man-down legal requirements for protecting lone workers in the us and canada? while there is no single federal law dedicated exclusively to lone worker safety, u.s. employers are still responsible for protecting these employees under the occupational safety and health act (osha). osha’s general duty clause requires all employers to provide a workplace free from recognized hazards, which includes risks faced by lone workers. lone workers may be at higher risk due to working alone, in remote locations, or in high-risk environments. to meet osha obligations, employers must: conduct hazard the land where our course exists today with thanks to the wortley family and friends. a 9 hole course was developed on what had previously been lane royd's deer park. the park is thought to have been originally laid out around 1800 when james archibald stuart wortley ii, first baron of wharncliffe married and settled in wortley. a club was formed in 1894 after the increasing popularity of the game amongst professional people in the area's wealthy families. when the clubhouse was built in 1911 the course was extended to a testing 18 holes and it was not long before wortley golf club gained a reputation for fast and undulating greens. there was great pride locally for a classic golf course in a predominantly rural, pastoral environment. an oasis of peace away from a busy world. there was every chance you would find francis john, the 2nd earl of wharncliffe and founding president of the golf club, teeing off with affluent friends. this whilst archibald ralph, francis john's eventual successor strolls with spaniel at heel out of the dense woodland that borders the course with a shooting party on a crisp saturday morning. over the years, wortley has maintained traditions and these historic sporting pursuits alongside a local syndicate that to this day shoot wild game and pheasant. you will find portraits of the first three earl presidents hanging in our clubhouse. in 1908, the extension to 18 holes was completed, almost certainly designed by alfred ernest turnell, club captain in 1905 and 1906, an esteemed buildings and golf course architect. in the late 1920’s the 3rd earl of wharncliffe decided to have the course re-designed. the project was undertaken by the most prominent golf course architect at that time, harry colt. wortley gained a reputation as a fair and
